Regulation: B.C. Reg. 132/2026
Made under: Personal Information Protection Act
Published in: No. 14 – B.C. Regs. 125 to 148, July 28, 2026
Deposit date: July 17, 2026

B.C. Reg. 132/2026, deposited July 17, 2026, under thePERSONAL INFORMATION PROTECTION ACT[section 58]. Order in Council 332/2026, approved and ordered July 17, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that, effective August 1, 2027, the Personal Information Protection Act Regulations, B.C. Reg. 473/2003, are amended as set out in the attached Schedule. — N. SHARMA,Attorney General and Deputy Premier; J. OSBORNE,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. 1	The Personal Information Protection Act Regulations, B.C. Reg. 473/2003, are amended by adding the following section: Request for correction of personal information – credit reporting agency 7(1)	For the purposes of section 24.1 (2) of the Act, the prescribed time within which a credit reporting agency must comply with section 24.1 (3) or (4) of the Act after receiving a request by an individual under section 24.1 (1) of the Act for the correction of personal information is 45 days. (2)	In addition to the requirements under section 24.1 (3) and (4) of the Act, a credit reporting agency, in responding to a request from an individual under section 24.1 (1) of the Act for the correction of personal information, must do the following: (a)	use its best efforts to check the accuracy and completeness of the information; (b)	within 45 days after receiving the request, report to the individual in writing respecting (i)	the correction of the information under section 24.1 (3) (a) of the Act, or (ii)	the annotation of the information under section 24.1 (4) of the Act. minutes_briefs.title: BC credit reporting agencies must fix or flag your personal information within 45 days starting August 1, 2027
minutes_briefs.summary: A new BC regulation sets a 45-day deadline for credit reporting agencies (companies like Equifax and TransUnion that collect and sell credit history) to respond when someone asks them to correct their personal information. Under the Personal Information Protection Act, the agency must either correct the information or add a note explaining the dispute, and must write back to the person within 45 days. The agency must also use its best efforts to check that the information is accurate and complete. The rule takes effect August 1, 2027.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If you report customer payment data to a credit reporting agency, update your records and dispute-handling process so corrections are confirmed and reported back within 45 days before August 1, 2027.

key_dates.label: BC credit reporting correction 45-day rule takes effect
